relatedSnapshot.title: Client Role Broken (Infinite Loop) & Missing Calendar Integration
relatedSnapshot.description:
**Description:** **Context:** The "Client" (or Member) user role is currently non-functional.

1. **Infinite Loop:** When a Client logs in, they are prompted to "Complete Onboarding." Clicking this (or Settings) redirects them back to the Dashboard repeatedly. They cannot access any settings.
2. **Calendar Blocking:** Because they cannot access Settings, they cannot connect their **Name 2/Outlook Calendar** or **Zoom Link**.

**Critical Impact:**

* **No Call Routing:** The AI SDR cannot book calls for specific clients because their calendars are not connected.
* **Security Risk:** The only workaround currently is to give clients "member access" to the agency account, which exposes all other data.
* **Global Calendar Bug:** If an Agency Admin adds a client's calendar to *their* own profile, it overrides the calendar for **ALL** workspaces.

**Requirement:**

1. **Fix the Redirect Loop:** Name 1 users to access their **Profile/Settings** page.
2. **Enable Integration:** Ensure Client users can connect their own Calendar, Meeting Links and Availability independently of the Agency Admin.
   
   
   OR we can add options for users to change calendar connection based on workspace if thats an easier fix

relatedSnapshot.title: Docs Gap: Onboarding answers don't carry over to a new workspace / white-label account (no guidance on reusing prior niche & offer answers)
relatedSnapshot.description:
DOCS GAP: There is no Help Center article explaining that onboarding answers do NOT carry over when a user starts fresh in a new workspace or a separate (white-label / partner) account, and no guidance on how to retrieve and reuse previously entered answers. Existing onboarding FAQs cover "can I run onboarding again", "wrong workspace", and "each workspace has its own onboarding progress", but none tell the user (a) that a separate account/instance requires re-onboarding, or (b) that they can view/copy their prior Niche & Offer answers from Settings → "Your Niche & Offer" in the original workspace and paste them into the new onboarding.

CUSTOMER CONTEXT: Customer (Name 3, <email>) completed onboarding on his original Acquisity account (under the Platform partner), then set up "his own Acquisity" — a separate white-label partner instance ("Company Five"). Signing into the new instance created a distinct account/workspace, so onboarding is prompted again. He asked whether there is any way to access his previous answers so he can copy/paste them into the new onboarding.

SUGGESTED CONTENT: Add an onboarding FAQ such as "I already onboarded — why do I have to do it again in my new workspace/account, and can I reuse my previous answers?" It should explain: (1) onboarding is scoped per workspace/account and does not automatically transfer, especially across separate/white-label accounts; (2) users can open their original workspace → Settings → "Your Niche & Offer" to view and copy their prior niche and offer responses, then paste them into the new onboarding; (3) note that separate white-label/partner accounts are distinct tenants even when they share the same email.

RELATED DOC(S):

* /docs/onboarding/faq/can-i-run-onboarding-again
* /docs/onboarding/faq/i-am-seeing-the-wrong-workspace
* /docs/onboarding/faq/what-gets-created-when-onboarding-finishes
* /docs/niche-researcher/faq/can-i-change-my-niche-later
  (Settings surface: /dashboard/[organizationSlug]/settings/niche-offer — "Your Niche & Offer", added in ENG-1723 / PR #1668)

FINDING: Not a bug. Expected behavior — onboarding and its answers (stored in organization_knowledge per org; also onboarding_session per user+org) are scoped per workspace/account and do not carry across a separate white-label/partner account. Verified in prod DB: the original account (Platform partner) has a completed onboarding with fully-populated organization_knowledge (niche/offer answers); the new "Company Five" partner account has an empty organization_knowledge and onboarding_status=reset, hence the re-prompt.

SLACK THREAD: <url:acquisityworkspace.slack.com>

relatedSnapshot.title: Onboarding a new workspace overwrites the account owner's name
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Completing onboarding for a new workspace overwrites the account-level user name. An agency or reseller owner who onboards a client workspace ends up with the client's name on their own account, and searching for the owner's name in the Admin Panel returns nothing.

## Problem

When an owner adds a client workspace and completes onboarding with the client's name, their own account name is replaced with the client's name. The owner then appears under the wrong name and their real name is not findable.

## Root cause

`apps/web/lib/onboarding/finalize-onboarding.ts` (lines 186-197) unconditionally sets `user.name = completedDraft.fullName` on every onboarding finalization. The account-level name should be set once and not overwritten by a secondary workspace's onboarding.

## Blast radius

115 users / 125 workspaces (counted 2026-09-10). Query: distinct users whose `name` equals the `organization_knowledge.business_info_form_data.fullName` of a workspace created after their earliest workspace, joined through `member` with `deleted_at IS NULL`.

## Proposed fix

`finalize-onboarding.ts` must not overwrite the account-level `user.name` when finalizing a secondary workspace's onboarding. Scope `fullName` to the workspace, or only set the account name on first onboarding.

## What's included

Code fix in the onboarding finalize transaction. Immediate name correction for affected accounts is a support data fix, handled separately.

## Regression seam

Onboarding finalization for a second workspace: the account owner's `user.name` must remain unchanged after finalizing a new workspace's onboarding.

## Done when

* Finalizing onboarding for a secondary workspace leaves the account owner's `user.name` unchanged.
* A regression test proves the name is not overwritten on secondary workspace onboarding.

## Reports

* ENG-13643

relatedSnapshot.title: Name 2 Calendar toggle switches re-enable themselves in workspace
relatedSnapshot.description:
Users report that when turning off a Name 2 Calendar inside a workspace, the calendar toggle automatically turns itself back on after being disabled. This occurs after disconnecting one Name 2 account and adding another for a specific workspace.

Context: reported while configuring calendars for multiple client workspaces (e.g. Company Seven, Company Eight).

User: <email>

Slack: <url:fegrowthpartner.slack.com>

---

After some discussion we found that we have a problem where email-calendar connections and settings are scoped to the user, but being updated on workspace settings.

The solution to this is the following:

### **Solution Overview**

Create a new workspace_member_settings table that stores workspace-specific overrides for user settings. The application will check this table first and fall back to the user's profile settings if no override exists.

**Key principle:** Calendar account connections remain at the user level. The new table only stores *preferences* about which existing accounts to use per workspace, not the account credentials themselves.

---

### **Implementation Steps**

#### 1\. Database Schema

Create a new table called workspace_member_settings in lib/db/schema/organization.ts with the following columns:

* id (UUID, primary key)
* memberId (UUID, foreign key to member table, unique, cascade delete)
* timezone (text, nullable) - Overrides user.timezone
* calendarAccountIds (UUID array, nullable) - References which integration_email_calendar_account records to use for this workspace. Null means use all.
* conferencingAccountId (UUID, nullable) - References which integration_conferencing_account to use
* conferencingLinkType (text, nullable) - Overrides user.conferencingLinkType
* conferencingStaticLink (text, nullable) - Overrides user.conferencingStaticLink
* Standard timestamps (createdAt, updatedAt)

Add appropriate relations to the member table.

#### 2\. Helper Service

Create a new service file lib/services/workspace-member-settings-service.ts with a function getEffectiveUserSettings(userId, organizationId) that:

1. Looks up the member record for the user + organization
2. Queries workspace_member_settings for that member
3. Queries the user table for default settings
4. Returns merged settings where workspace overrides take precedence over user defaults
5. Returns null for calendar account IDs if no preference is set (meaning "use all")

#### 3\. Update Scheduling Repository

Modify lib/scheduling/repositories/scheduling-repository.ts:

* Update getUserWithIntegrations to accept an optional organizationId parameter
* When organizationId is provided, use the helper service to get effective settings
* Filter calendar accounts based on workspace preferences if set
* Use workspace timezone if set, otherwise user timezone

#### 4\. Update Services That Use Timezone/Calendar Settings

Update the following files to pass organizationId and use effective settings:

* lib/scheduling/services/booking-service.ts
* lib/scheduling/services/calendar-integration.ts
* lib/scheduling/services/calendar-event-builder.ts
* lib/scheduling/services/availability-scheduler.ts

Review and update as needed:

* trpc/routers/appointments.ts
* trpc/routers/integrations/email-calendar.ts
* trpc/routers/integrations/conferencing.ts
* Inngest functions that reference timezone (search for .timezone in the codebase)

#### 5\. Create tRPC Router

Create a new router trpc/routers/workspace-member-settings.ts with procedures:

* get - Fetch current workspace settings for the authenticated user in the active organization
* update - Create or update workspace settings (upsert by memberId)
* reset - Delete workspace settings to revert to profile defaults

Add the router to the main router index.

#### 6\. Settings UI

Create a new settings page at app/(saas)/dashboard/(sidebar)/(organization-settings)/\[organizationSlug\]/settings/calendar-preferences/page.tsx with:

**Timezone Section:**

* Show current effective timezone with indicator if using profile default
* Dropdown to select workspace-specific timezone
* Option to reset to profile default

**Calendar Accounts Section:**

* List all connected calendar accounts from the user's profile
* Name 23 to select which accounts are active for this workspace
* When none selected or all selected, use profile default (all accounts)
* Clear indication of which accounts are active

**Conferencing Section:**

* Show current conferencing preference with indicator if using profile default
* Options to select workspace-specific conferencing account
* Static link field if applicable
* Option to reset to profile default

Add navigation link to the settings sidebar in the settings layout.

#### 7\. Name 22

Modify components/calendar/timezone-change-dialog.tsx to:

* Check workspace settings first when comparing timezones
* When user confirms timezone change, update workspace settings (not user profile) if in a workspace context

---

### **Acceptance Criteria**

- [ ] User can set a different timezone per workspace
- [ ] User can select which calendar accounts are active per workspace
- [ ] User can set different conferencing preferences per workspace
- [ ] When no workspace preference is set, user profile settings are used (backward compatible)
- [ ] Settings UI clearly indicates when using profile defaults vs. workspace overrides
- [ ] User can reset workspace settings to use profile defaults
- [ ] Existing users with no workspace settings continue to work as before
- [ ] Scheduling/booking flow respects workspace-specific settings
- [ ] Calendar availability checks use correct accounts per workspace

---

### **Out of Scope**

* Migrating existing user settings to workspace settings
* Work hours per workspace (can be added later using same pattern)
* Bulk management of settings across workspaces

---

### **Testing Notes**

* Test with a user in multiple workspaces with different settings
* Test fallback behavior when workspace settings don't exist
* Test that calendar connections still work at user level
* Test scheduling flow uses correct timezone and calendar accounts per workspace

relatedSnapshot.title: Customer report: "Your Niche & Offer" says to complete onboarding despite completed onboarding
relatedSnapshot.description:
Source: Intercom conversation <url:app.intercom.com>

Claim: In a workspace whose onboarding is already completed, Settings -> Your Niche & Offer shows "No niche selected. Please complete the onboarding process first." instead of the niche/offer form, so the customer cannot set her own niche, even though Niche Researcher and Offer Creator runs succeed.

Bounded conversation context: Customer opened the conversation on 2026-09-15 23:25 UTC reporting that the Niche Researcher keeps returning niches she does not want and that Settings -> Your Niche & Offer will not let her set her own niche because it says onboarding is incomplete. She says she finished onboarding at least three times, used Reset Workspace Onboarding, and once saw "could not save onboarding progress"; the support agent also told her onboarding "was not successfully completed". Screenshots of the settings and onboarding screens are attached to the conversation. Two workspaces of the same user are involved.

Current production evidence (read 2026-09-16): for both workspaces organization.onboarding_status = 'completed' while organization_knowledge.niche_agent_status = 'pending', selected_niche_id is NULL and generated_niches is NULL. In the same window 9 niche_researcher and 4 offer_creator submissions for those workspaces completed successfully, with results saved.

Suspected path: apps/web/lib/onboarding/finalize-onboarding.ts writes only businessInfoFormData and sets onboarding_status = completed, so no niche is ever generated into organization_knowledge; apps/web/trpc/routers/organizations.ts getNicheOfferSettings returns selectedNiche null whenever selected_niche_id is null; apps/web/components/organization/niche-offer-settings-card.tsx renders the misleading onboarding message on that null.
